newsitem.title: USA: NASD charges Sterling Foster of fraud - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: NASD charges Sterling Foster of fraud - newspaper.

text.p: The enforcement division of the National Association of Securities Dealers has accused a NASD marketmaker of defrauding customers of $53 million in three initial public offerings in 1995, the Washington Post reported on Wednesday.

The complaint, issued by NASD Regulation Inc, accuses Sterling Foster & Co and 15 of its executives of supposedly defrauding investors by manipulating the market for three offerings, namely Advanced Voice Technologies Inc, Com/Tech Communication Technologies Inc, and Embryo Development Corp.

Under the rules of the NASD, the merits of the complaints will be weighed by a three-person committee of the NASD. A finding against Sterling Foster could be appealed to the NASD, then the Securities and Exchange Commission, and eventually federal courts.
